name: Śrī Puruṣottama Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: before sannyāsa Śrīnivāsācārya (Vyāsarāja Maṭha's own record); disciple of Jayadhvaja Tīrtha (Jayadharma in the Gauḍīya list); ordained at Purī as the tenth pontiff of the line later called the Vyāsarāja Maṭha; his seat Channapatna / Abbūr, on the Kaṇva (Karnataka). Disciple and successor: Brahmaṇya Tīrtha. Tradition holds that he did not die but vanished into tapasyā in Puruṣottama Guhā, a cave near Abbūr; locally called Maḍi Svāmī, Huli Svāmī («Tiger Svāmī») and Guhe Svāmī («Cave Svāmī»).

name: Rāghava Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: also Rāghava Gosāi, Rāghava Paṇḍita; Campakalatā, one of Śrī Rādhā's eight chief sakhīs. He lived in a cave at the southern end of Govardhana, near Apsarā-kuṇḍa and Pūñchari (Bhakti-ratnākara 5); already living there, with his book written, when the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā was finished in 1576. His closest companion was Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī. At Jīva Gosvāmī's request he guided Śrīnivāsa and Narottama around Vraja-maṇḍala. His Kṛṣṇa-bhakti-ratna-prakāśa is in six chapters called «jewels». No old source names his guru.

name: Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita
add: Nandgram Dham: the seventh branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.24); Pāṇihāṭi, near Sodpur, is a day's journey from Navadvīpa. His sub-branch Makaradhvaja Kara was the superintendent of the bags (jhāli).

name: Raghunandana Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: his father Mukunda dāsa was a royal physician and the elder brother of Narahari Sarakāra. Named in Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.78–79 and Madhya 11.92. He worshipped the family Deities, Śrī Gopīnātha and Gaura-Gopāla, at Śrīkhaṇḍa; his son Kānāi Ṭhākura followed him in that service.

name: Śrī Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: born Raghunātha Bhaṭṭācārya, c. 1503–1505 in Vārāṇasī; sent to study under Rūpa and Sanātana in Vṛndāvana. He recited the Bhāgavatam «in a voice as sweet as a cuckoo's». He served Govinda, whose temple his disciples built by his inspiration. He left this world c. 1579 at Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

name: Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: the only son of Govardhana Majumadāra; born c. 1494 (sources vary). Chief works: Stavāvalī (with Manaḥ-śikṣā and Vilāpa-kusumāñjali), Dāna-keli-cintāmaṇi, Muktā-carita. Traditionally left this world in 1586 at Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

name: Raghupati Upādhyāya
add: Nandgram Dham: a brāhmaṇa scholar, poet and householder of Tirhut (Tīrabhukti). His discipleship of Mādhavendra Purī comes from the Gauḍīya-bhāṣya on the Caitanya-bhāgavata (Ādi 2.31). Three of his Sanskrit verses are kept in Rūpa Gosvāmī's Padyāvalī (82, 99, 126). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śrī Rājendra Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: independent Dvaita sources name his guru Vidyādhirāja Tīrtha, seventh pontiff of Madhva's original maṭha at Uḍupī (the Gauḍīya list: Vidyānidhi). He founded the Rājendra Tīrtha (Pūrvādi) Maṭha, later called the Vyāsarāja Maṭha after his fourth successor Vyāsa Tīrtha, and headed it c. 1402–1440 (B. N. K. Sharma). Disciples: Jayadharma (Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha), and Viṣṇudāsācārya, a dialectician of North India.

name: Rāmacandra Kavirāja
add: Nandgram Dham: works Smaraṇa-camatkāra, Smaraṇa-darpaṇa, Siddhānta-candrikā and a life of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. His samādhi is at Dhīra-samīra, Vṛndāvana, beside Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's.

name: Rāmacandra Purī
add: Nandgram Dham: after his criticism the Lord cut His meals to a quarter, later raised to half at the devotees' request (Antya 8, «Rāmacandra Purī criticizes the Lord»). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Rāmadāsa Brāhmaṇa
add: Nandgram Dham: a brāhmaṇa the Lord met at Siddhavaṭa, near the Śrī Raṅganātha temple, on His South India tour; he had chanted Lord Rāmacandra's name since childhood, and after seeing the Lord found Kṛṣṇa's name on his tongue instead of Rāma's (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9.17–38). His birth, death, family and the rest of his life are not recorded.

name: Rāmadāsa Bipra
add: Nandgram Dham: a learned brāhmaṇa, lifelong chanter of Rāma's name; absorbed in Rāma's pastimes he forgot to cook; later the Lord gave him an original leaf of the Kūrma Purāṇa with His own hand (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9.178–217). His birth, death and family are not recorded.

name: Rāmadāsa Viśvāsa
add: Nandgram Dham: a secretary in a royal administration; a lifelong worshipper of Lord Rāmacandra (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 13.89–112).

name: Rāmānanda Rāya
add: Nandgram Dham: also Rāya Rāmānanda, Rāma Rāya. He wrote the Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka, a Sanskrit drama of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes in Vṛndāvana; in Purī he served the Lord for decades with Svarūpa Dāmodara.

name: Śrī Raṅga Purī
add: Nandgram Dham: his sannyāsī godbrothers include Īśvara Purī, Paramānanda Purī and Rāmacandra Purī. Paṇḍharpur is on the Bhīmā; the meeting is told again in Madhya 1.113. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Rasikānanda Prabhu
add: Nandgram Dham: he served Rādhā-Govinda at Gopīvallabhapura and later Rādhā-Rasika Rāya at the Kuñja Maṭha in Purī; he left this world at the Kṣīra-corā Gopīnātha temple, Remuṇā.
